ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: On 5 April 1242 Alexander Nevsky's Novgorodians defeated the Livonian Order on frozen Lake Peipus, which checked the crusaders' expansion into Russian lands.
In 1658 Charles X Gustav marched across the frozen Belts and forced the Treaty of Roskilde on Denmark; in 1709 defeat at Poltava broke Swedish power.
In Europe's coldest winter of the past 500 years, storms and frosts killed thousands in the Swedish army invading Russia, contributing to its defeat at Poltava.
George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River
On the night of 25–26 December 1776 Washington led a column across the icy Delaware in rain, sleet and snow to surprise the Hessians at Trenton.
In winter quarters from December 1777 an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 soldiers died of disease, possibly made worse by malnutrition and cold, wet weather.
The empire proclaimed in 1721 after the defeat of Sweden was invaded in 1812 by Napoleon's Grande Armée, which was destroyed in the winter retreat.
The Russian army retreated and fought at Borodino, Moscow burned after its occupation, and Napoleon's retreat in winter destroyed most of his army.
Independent since 1917, Finland was attacked by the Soviet Union in 1939 and fought the Winter War, losing Karelia but keeping its independence.
From December 1939 Finnish ski troops cut two road-bound Soviet divisions into isolated pockets in the forests of north-eastern Finland and destroyed them.
The Germans decided to starve the city: many residents starved in the winter of 1941–1942, and supplies crossed Lake Ladoga in winter over the Road of Life on the ice.
